projects.title: Industrial Multi-Gateway Wi-Fi Mesh Traffic-Steering Platform
projects.summary: This project developed an OpenWrt-based multi-gateway Wi-Fi mesh platform for industrial environments where wired backhaul is limited or costly. The system dynamically steers Internet-bound connections through selected gateways while retaining compatibility with standard Wi-Fi clients and commodity routers.
highlights: Connection-level gateway selection and traffic steering across multiple Internet gateways.
Kernel and user-space packet-processing pipeline using Netfilter/NFQUEUE, routing, NAT state, and Netlink-based control.
Efficient asymmetric processing: outgoing LAN-to-Internet packets are classified and steered, while return traffic follows the established route without repeated application-level filtering.
Prototype validation using real network measurements, traffic logs, and multi-gateway test scenarios.
deliverables: Kernel flow-state tables and C-based Netlink control software.
Experimental evaluation tools, measurement datasets, and technical documentation.

projects.title: Cost-Aware Load Balancing and Seamless Mobility for Cellular-Enabled Wi-Fi Mesh Networks
projects.summary: This project investigated the use of multiple cellular-enabled routers as Internet gateways for large-scale Wi-Fi mesh networks. A centrally controlled architecture was developed to balance traffic across cellular gateways while considering both cellular data quotas and multi-hop forwarding cost. The system also supports station mobility without interrupting active TCP connections.
highlights: SDN-inspired control architecture implemented on commodity Linux-based routers.
Quadratic Programming-Assisted Load Balancing (QPLB) for joint optimization of gateway quota usage and mesh forwarding cost.
Concurrent utilization of multiple cellular gateways.
On-demand per-connection forwarding that preserves active TCP sessions when a client roams between mesh nodes.
No modifications required to client devices or underlying Wi-Fi standards.
Evaluation showed a 58%–83% reduction in cellular-quota imbalance and a 34% reduction in median byte-weighted hop count compared with representative baselines.
deliverables: QPLB optimization algorithm and simulation framework.
Fully functional prototype on off-the-shelf wireless routers.
